paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: Training loss curves for the post-training setting.
model_annotation: The plot shows training loss as a function of iteration for several SepLLM post-training runs and a baseline reference. The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from 95,000 to 127,000 iterations, with regularly spaced tick labels every 5,000 iterations (95,000, 100,000, 105,000, …, 125,000). The y-axis is labeled “Loss,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 2.0 to 3.0 with tick marks at 0.2 intervals (2.0, 2.2, 2.4, 2.6, 2.8, 3.0). Three solid lines show loss decreasing over iterations: a magenta solid line labeled “SepLLM (n=64, larger lr)” starts near the top of the axis around 3.0 at ~95k iterations, drops steeply to about 2.45 by ~100k, and then continues to decline more gradually to about 2.21–2.22 by ~127k; a blue solid line labeled “SepLLM (n=128)” begins around 3.0 near ~95k, decreases to roughly 2.58–2.60 by ~100k, and then tapers to about 2.28–2.29 by ~127k; an orange solid line labeled “SepLLM (n=64)” similarly starts near 3.0 at ~95k, falls to around 2.60 by ~100k, and trends down to about 2.29–2.30 by ~127k, with a narrow upward spike just after 100k iterations reaching roughly 2.8 before returning to the surrounding trajectory. A red dashed horizontal line labeled “Vanilla before post-training” is constant across the full x-range at approximately 2.35 loss.
